title: Hassan Allam and Sterling & Wilson win US$200m first phase of Humain-center3 Riyadh data centre
description: A joint venture won an estimated SR750m ($200m) contract to build phase one of a Humain and center3 data centre in Riyadh. Phase one has 16.2MW IT load over 16 months, rising to 50MW in phase two, within a wider programme MEED puts at up to 1GW.
quote: The first phase will have an IT load capacity of 16.2MW, with overall capacity reaching 50MW in the second phase.
analysis: A 50MW Riyadh site implies standby/prime generator blocks that will be specified during the 16-month phase-one build, and the EPC pair (Sterling & Wilson is an electrical specialist) is the buying party. Cummins Arabia should open a data-centre power-package conversation with the JV and center3 now, before genset specs are frozen.

title: Microsoft sets November 2026 launch for Saudi Arabia East cloud region
description: Announced at LEAP 2026, the Eastern Province region will have three Azure availability zones and open in November 2026. Microsoft cites an IDC estimate of $44bn new Saudi revenue in 2027-2030, with the region about 13.4% of it.
quote: Located in the Eastern Province, the region will comprise three Azure Availability Zones
analysis: With launch weeks away, the near-term genset value for Cummins Arabia is service, load-bank testing and capacity additions at the Eastern Province sites rather than new-build supply (estimate: construction was reported complete earlier). Pitch O&M and capacity-add upgrades to the facility operators before the November go-live.

title: Aramco nears award of Jafurah fifth-phase gas compression EPC, L&T in advanced talks
description: MEED reports Aramco and L&T have reached an advanced negotiation stage on EPC of three gas compression plants of up to 200 million cf/d each. Bids closed 19 July; Jafurah is a $100bn capex programme.
quote: Negotiations between Aramco and L&T have reached an advanced stage
analysis: Gas compression plants need emergency and black-start power, usually bought by the EPC contractor from Aramco-approved vendors, so the award fixes who Cummins Arabia must approach. Confirm the Aramco vendor-list status of Cummins gensets and contact L&T Hydrocarbon procurement once the award is public.

title: Contractors register interest in Jafurah sixth expansion phase; L&T already working on draft award
description: Contractors expressed interest to Aramco in another three-plant gas compression phase, each plant up to 200 million cf/d. MEED says Aramco issued a solicitation of interest in August and the formal award and FID are pending.
quote: Contractors have expressed interest to Saudi Aramco in the next major expansion phase
analysis: Jafurah is a multi-year chain of phases, so genset and emergency power demand repeats with each package. Track the sixth phase award as an annuity-type opportunity and register Cummins Arabia with the same EPC contractors.

title: RTCC/Ictas JV wins US$214m King Salman airport private aviation terminal
description: An Al-Rashid Trading & Contracting and IC Ictas JV won an estimated SR800m ($214m) contract for the private aviation terminal at King Salman International airport. The airport covers about 57 sq km with a 100 million passenger target by 2030.
quote: The contract was awarded to a joint venture of Riyadh-based Al-Rashid Trading & Contracting (RTCC) and Turkiye's IC Ictas.
analysis: Airport terminals carry life-safety standby generation, bought through the main contractor and MEP subcontractors. Cummins Arabia should reach RTCC and the MEP package holders and include the new airport's central power plant as a separate lead.

title: Saudi Royal Aviation aviation complex (SR3bn) bids were due 8 October at Riyadh's King Salman airport
description: SRA tendered an estimated SR3bn ($817m) aviation complex in August, with 30 landside and 15 airside buildings. Bids were due 8 October.
quote: Government-owned aviation organisation Saudi Royal Aviation (SRA) tendered the contract in August.
analysis: An award is likely in the coming months and will produce a standby-power scope for 45 buildings. Identify the bidders now and offer packaged gensets to the likely MEP partners.

title: Dubai RTA appoints Aecom to design Route 2020 metro extension to Al-Maktoum airport
description: RTA awarded a design contract for a 3 km, two-station extension linking the Expo 2020 station to Al-Maktoum airport's West Terminal. Egis had earlier been the lowest bidder at AED232.6m according to a related MEED report.
quote: The extension will run about 3 kilometres (km) and include two stations.
analysis: Only design is awarded, so genset demand (station and tunnel emergency power) is 2027 or later. Keep it on the Dubai transport watch list and note it as a second Al-Maktoum airport enabler.

title: Saudi new Government Tenders and Procurement Law approved 5 Aug 2026; local-content regime stays in force
description: A Clyde & Co note says the Council of Ministers approved a new GTPL on 5 August 2026 while the 2019 local-content preference rules (10% evaluation price preference for national products, mandatory list) still apply. Contractors face local-content plans, reporting and penalties.
quote: Saudi Arabia has established a comprehensive legal framework governing local content in public procurement.
analysis: Government genset tenders can favour national products by a 10% evaluation preference, which hurts imported brands that lack Saudi content. Cummins Arabia should document its Saudi-assembled or local-content share and check the LCGPA mandatory list for generator sets.

title: Kuwait reviews bids for 3,400MW of power and water PPP projects; contracts possible Q1 2027
description: Joint PPP Authority and MEW committees are evaluating the 1,100MW Shagaya solar phase, a 500MW second Shagaya project and the 1,800MW Al-Khairan IWPP (33 MIGD). If technical evaluations finish by end-2026, contracts could be signed in Q1 2027.
quote: Two international consortia are competing for the project
analysis: These are IPP/IWPP builds with 30 to 54 month schedules, so genset demand is auxiliary and black-start power in 2028-2030, procured by the winning consortium's EPC. Meanwhile Kuwait's supply gap keeps demand for standby and rental power high, so Cummins Arabia's Kuwait rental and standby pipeline should be prioritised ahead of the new-build wave.

title: Hormuz shipping stalls again: five vessels transit in a day, Brent near US$107, Iran offers 7-day reopening plan
description: Kpler data cited by Gulf News show five commodity vessels crossed Hormuz on Saturday 26 Sep versus 31 the prior weekend, with no transits on Sunday. Brent gained about 3% to near $107.30 on 28 Sep.
quote: No transits were recorded on Sunday in the preliminary data.
analysis: Inbound engines, alternators and switchgear for Cummins Arabia in Jebel Ali and Dammam face freight and insurance delays and cost, which can lengthen genset lead times on project deliveries. Review committed delivery dates and safety stock for the data-centre and utility orders due before year end.

title: Hormuz flows recover to about 14m bpd per US, but diesel stays 'very high' and Houthi attack hits Riyadh
description: US Energy Secretary Wright put Gulf crude flows incl. bypass pipelines at 80-90% of pre-war levels, while Kpler showed Hormuz exports at just under 9m bpd in September (44% of February). The article reports a Houthi attack in Riyadh that killed 12 or 13 and injured about 300.
quote: The challenge is still here and the challenge is still ahead of us," he said.
analysis: High diesel prices raise fuel cost for customers running standby and prime sets and push interest toward gas or dual-fuel and bigger storage, while attacks on Riyadh raise the chance of grid and facility hardening demand. Cummins Arabia should prepare a resilience offer (autonomy, fuel storage, dual-fuel) for data-centre, hospital and utility accounts.

title: Al-Mansouria wins US$105m contract to finish 563-bed Taiba University Hospital in Medina
description: A SR396m ($105.6m) contract covers structure, MEP and clinical fit-out for a stalled 563-bed teaching hospital, with three years duration and late-2029 delivery. The original SR500m contract dated from December 2011.
quote: The contract duration is three years, with delivery targeted for late 2029.
analysis: Completion of MEP and medical gas works means hospital standby generation (typically N+1 sets) will be bought by Al-Mansouria's MEP subcontractors within the next 12 to 18 months. Cummins Arabia should contact the contractor and the Medina consultant to be named on the genset spec.

title: Saudi MoD tenders next phase of King Saud Air Base (Hafr Al-Batin); bids due 20 Oct
description: The Ministry of Defence and Aviation is tendering a three-year phase covering headquarters, operations, weapons areas, residential and airfield facilities on a 383 sq km site. First-phase contracts were about SR6.6bn ($1.8bn).
quote: Contractors have been given until 20 October to submit their bids.
analysis: Air bases need prime and standby power and are normally supplied through the winning contractors and military power packages, so the award will set who Cummins Arabia should approach in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027. Identify the bidding teams after 20 October and check Cummins Arabia's military-project references.

title: Houthi strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid airport kill 13; Saudi airport operations suspended
description: MEED reports two weekend strikes on King Khalid International killed 13 and injured 320, with the 10 October terminal strike killing 12. GACA's weekly toll for attacks on Saudi airports is 19 dead and more than 350 injured.
quote: Airport operations were suspended pending a damage assessment.
analysis: Strikes on airports and the capital can delay Riyadh airport and giga-project schedules and staff mobilisation, which pushes back genset deliveries; they also raise demand for hardened standby power at critical sites. Cummins Arabia should check site-access and delivery risk on live Riyadh orders and offer emergency rental sets for damaged facilities.

title: Neom pivots to industry: Oxagon AI data centre breaks ground at 100MW, targeted for 2028
description: MEED says the Oxagon AI data-centre campus broke ground on a first 100MW phase backed by $5bn, targeted for 2028, and that Saudi contract awards reached $68bn so far this year. The $8.5bn Neom green hydrogen plant was commissioned in August.
quote: These developments reflect a kingdom recalibrating rather than retreating
analysis: Demand at Neom is moving from residential giga-project builds to industrial and AI loads, with the 100MW first phase not live until 2028, so genset orders come late and via the data-centre developer and EPC. Cummins Arabia should reposition its Neom account from MEP packages to the Oxagon AI campus and track the EPC award.

title: Diriyah awards US$729m of hotel and residential contracts to UCC Saudi and a local JV
description: Diriyah Company awarded two contracts worth more than SR2.7bn ($729m): $375m to UCC Saudi and $353m to a Almajal Alarabi / Man Enterprise Al-Saudia JV for hotels and branded residences. Scope includes MEP and fit-out in Diriyah Square.
quote: The Diriyah masterplan envisages the city as a cultural and lifestyle tourism destination.
analysis: Hotel and residential towers need standby generation, specified during the MEP phase that the two awarded contractors are starting. Cummins Arabia should approach both MEP packages with a standard hospitality genset offer.

title: Kuwait tenders 24-inch gas export pipeline from BS-171; bids due 5 January 2027
description: A tender covers a 24-inch gas export line from the BS-171 acid-gas facility, about 80 km to the ISC facility. A preliminary online meeting is set for mid-November.
analysis: A pipeline contract carries small remote-site power needs, but it signals continued Kuwaiti upstream spending despite the conflict. Add it to the Kuwait oil and gas watch list and brief the bidding contractors on Cummins Arabia's field-power and service offer.

title: Six contractor groups prequalify for AED34bn Dubai Metro Gold Line
description: Six consortiums submitted prequalification statements on 9 October for the fully underground 42km, 18-station line, costed at about AED34bn ($9.2bn), with completion targeted for September 2032.
quote: The project is scheduled to be completed in September 2032.
analysis: An underground metro needs emergency and tunnel-ventilation backup power at 18 stations, but orders are 2028 onwards and sit with the winning consortium's MEP contractors. Cummins Arabia should map the six consortium members now and engage the favourites before the tender stage.

title: Kuwait approves KD5.52m of high-voltage cable maintenance to protect summer 2027 peak
description: Kuwait's electricity ministry cleared two high-voltage transformer cable maintenance and repair projects worth KD5.52m in the northern and southern regions. The work targets summer 2027 and aims to reduce outage risk at peak demand.
quote: The work is also intended to reduce the risk of outages during periods of peak demand.
analysis: With no large new generation online before 2027-28 and a stressed grid, Kuwaiti commercial and industrial customers keep relying on standby and rental gensets through summer 2027. Cummins Arabia should build rental and standby capacity in Kuwait before April 2027.
